domain_label: Inference Serving & Quantization (Training & Inference Infrastructure subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is LLM inference serving, quantization methods, and multi-specialist LoRA serving
target workload is orchestrated specialist LLMs on GPU infrastructure
exclusions: model training and fine-tuning internals (covered by ftune__ KBs)
orchestration DAG and routing logic above serving layer (covered by orch__ KBs)
security and access control beyond serving isolation

competency_questions.question: How is the serving framework selected for specialist LLM deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVE_ARCH covers framework options, criteria, and decision factors

competency_questions.question: What latency metrics are measured and what are the SLA validation criteria?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCH_SERVE and LATENCY_PROFILING define TTFT/TPOT and SLA gates

competency_questions.question: How does PagedAttention and continuous batching increase serving throughput?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KV_CACHE and CONT_BATCH explain virtual paging and iteration scheduling

competency_questions.question: What is the mechanism and memory benefit of KV cache paging and quantization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KV_CACHE covers PagedAttention; KV_QUANT covers FP8 quantization of KV tensors

competency_questions.question: How are GPTQ and AWQ post-training quantization applied and how is quality degradation evaluated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANT_GPTQ, QUANT_AWQ, QUANT_QUALITY cover calibration, bit-width, and evaluation

competency_questions.question: When is GGUF/llama.cpp appropriate vs vLLM, and what quality/throughput tradeoffs apply?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANT_GGUF and LOCAL_VS_HOSTED define GGUF scope and decision criteria

competency_questions.question: How does GGUF k-quant tier selection affect local inference quality and throughput?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANT_GGUF covers k-quant tiers and acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: How are many LoRA specialist adapters served on a single base model without per-specialist GPU?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LORA_HOTSWAP covers adapter LRU cache, swap latency, and S-LoRA

competency_questions.question: How is request routing to the correct specialist adapter implemented and validated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTER_DISPATCH covers classifier, dispatch, fallback, and accuracy gate

competency_questions.question: When does self-hosted serving become more cost-effective than hosted API for specialists?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_VS_HOSTED and AUTOSCALE define TCO model and breakeven analysis

competency_questions.question: How is autoscaling configured to balance cost and cold-start latency for specialist endpoints?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUTOSCALE covers scale-to-zero, readiness, and latency constraints

competency_questions.question: What quantized inference kernels are needed and how is throughput recovery from quantization validated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANT_KERNEL covers kernel selection and MFU acceptance test

glossary.definition: time-to-first-token; latency from request arrival to first output token generated
time-per-output-token; inter-token latency during decode phase
virtual memory paging system for KV cache blocks eliminating fragmentation in variable-length sequence serving
iteration-level scheduling that dynamically fills batch slots as sequences complete, eliminating padding waste of static batching
post-training quantization using second-order layer-wise weight compression (Frantar et al. 2022)
activation-aware weight quantization protecting salient channels by activation magnitude calibration
llama.cpp binary format for quantized model weights supporting CPU and hybrid CPU+GPU inference
low-rank adaptation; lightweight fine-tune adding rank-decomposed weight matrices to frozen base model
sharding individual weight matrices across GPUs so each GPU holds a partition; requires all-reduce for each layer
draft model proposes multiple tokens per step; target model verifies in parallel; accepted tokens emitted with identical output distribution

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for LLM inference serving and quantization work units in absence of supplied datasets
grounding_limits: key papers: Kwon et al. 2023 (vLLM/PagedAttention), Frantar et al. 2022 (GPTQ)

nodes.definition: Select and configure an LLM serving framework (vLLM, TGI, llama.cpp, or custom) matching throughput, latency, and cost requirements for specialist model deployment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU architecture or serving framework major version change

pros.claim: vLLM continuous batching multiplies throughput vs naive single-request serving
pros.example: vLLM achieves 10-24x throughput vs HuggingFace generate() on A100

cons.claim: Framework lock-in makes switching costly once models and tooling integrate
cons.example: TGI-specific gRPC API requires client rewrite to migrate to vLLM

failure_modes: serving engine incompatible with quantized model format
memory over-commit OOM at peak batch
CUDA driver/toolkit version mismatch causing silent correctness failures
acceptance_tests: throughput >=target tok/s at p50 latency budget
OOM-free at 2x expected concurrent requests
output matches reference fp16 within tolerance

nodes.definition: Implement iteration-level scheduling (continuous batching) to fill GPU compute with in-flight requests dynamically rather than padding static batches.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scheduler policy changes or new token-streaming latency requirements

pros.claim: Eliminates GPU idle time between batches; doubles to triples effective throughput
pros.example: vLLM scheduler preempts finished sequences and inserts new requests mid-decode

cons.claim: Head-of-line blocking by long sequences inflates p99 latency for short requests
cons.example: 32k-token completion delays 64 short queries in same batch

failure_modes: starvation of short requests behind long sequence
incorrect KV eviction during preemption
token accounting error corrupting sequence length
acceptance_tests: p99 latency < 3x p50 under sustained load
scheduler throughput >= 95% of theoretical peak

nodes.definition: Manage KV cache memory with PagedAttention virtual paging to eliminate fragmentation and maximize concurrency under variable sequence lengths.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context length increases or model architecture changes attention layout

pros.claim: PagedAttention reduces KV memory waste from ~70% to <4% enabling 2-4x more concurrent sequences
pros.example: Kwon et al. 2023 show near-zero fragmentation on A100

cons.claim: Block table management adds implementation complexity; bugs cause incorrect attention
cons.example: Wrong block pointer silently corrupts generation output

failure_modes: block table corruption causing attention to wrong tokens
OOM when block pool under-provisioned
eviction policy thrashing under mixed long/short requests
acceptance_tests: KV memory utilization >85% under target concurrency
no attention corruption vs reference on 500 sequences
eviction/swap rate <5% under normal load

nodes.definition: Apply GPTQ (Frantar et al. 2022) layer-wise second-order weight quantization to compress LLMs to 4-bit or 8-bit with minimal perplexity loss.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new quantization algorithm supersedes GPTQ or calibration data domain shifts

pros.claim: 4-bit GPTQ reduces VRAM 4x with <1 PPL loss on 7B+ models enabling single-GPU 70B serving
pros.example: LLaMA-65B in 4-bit fits A100-80GB vs OOM at fp16

cons.claim: Calibration dataset quality critically affects task-specific quality; wrong calibration set degrades specialist tasks
cons.example: Code-specialized calibration set needed for coding specialists

failure_modes: calibration data distribution mismatch causes task-specific quality collapse
incorrect groupsize causes asymmetric quantization error
outlier channels unhandled causing NaN weights
acceptance_tests: PPL delta <1.0 vs fp16 on held-out corpus
task accuracy delta <3% on target benchmark
4-bit model serves without NaN or inf values
revisit_triggers: new quantization scheme (AWQ/GGUF) shows superior quality

nodes.definition: Apply AWQ activation-aware weight quantization that protects salient channels identified by activation magnitude, achieving better quality than GPTQ at same bit-width.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: AWQ hardware kernel support expands or better calibration strategy found

pros.claim: AWQ outperforms GPTQ on instruction-following tasks by preserving activation-critical weights
pros.example: AWQ-4bit shows +2-3% MT-Bench vs GPTQ-4bit same model

cons.claim: Requires per-model activation calibration pass; slower quantization than GPTQ
cons.example: AWQ calibration on 70B model takes 30min vs 15min GPTQ

failure_modes: salient channel identification fails on atypical architectures
hardware kernel missing for AWQ on target GPU
groupsize-hardware mismatch causing slow dequantization
acceptance_tests: task accuracy delta <2% vs fp16
AWQ kernel throughput >=GPTQ at same batch size
revisit_triggers: new model family with different activation statistics
target GPU lacks fused AWQ kernel

nodes.definition: Convert and quantize models to GGUF format (k-quants) for llama.cpp local deployment on CPU+GPU hybrid or edge devices with minimal infrastructure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new llama.cpp k-quant tier outperforms current or target hardware changes

pros.claim: GGUF Q4_K_M enables 70B model inference on consumer 64GB RAM with no GPU required
pros.example: llama.cpp Q4_K_M on M2 Ultra achieves 12 tok/s for 70B

cons.claim: CPU/hybrid inference throughput 5-20x lower than GPU vLLM; unsuitable for high-concurrency serving
cons.example: Q4_K_M on CPU: 8 tok/s vs vLLM A100: 120 tok/s at batch=1

failure_modes: quantization tier selection too aggressive causing visible quality degradation
GGUF format version incompatibility
CPU BLAS library mismatch causing slow inference
acceptance_tests: GGUF loads and generates on target hardware without error
PPL delta <1.5 vs fp16 for selected k-quant tier
revisit_triggers: latency budget tightens beyond CPU capability

nodes.definition: Shard model weights across multiple GPUs via tensor parallelism (column/row splitting of weight matrices) or pipeline parallelism to serve models exceeding single-GPU VRAM.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU interconnect topology changes or model size class crosses single-GPU boundary

pros.claim: Enables 70B+ model serving without quantization at fp16 quality across 4-8 GPUs
pros.example: LLaMA-70B on 4xA100 via TP=4 at fp16 with 80 tok/s

cons.claim: All-reduce communication overhead on NVLink-less multi-node scales poorly beyond TP=8
cons.example: TP=16 on 2 nodes with InfiniBand shows 30% throughput degradation vs TP=8 single node

failure_modes: NCCL deadlock from rank synchronization error
unequal shard size for non-divisible head counts
pipeline bubble causing throughput collapse
acceptance_tests: model loads across all ranks without error
throughput scales >=70% of linear up to TP=4
output matches single-GPU reference within fp16 tolerance
revisit_triggers: model head count not divisible by TP degree
new Flash Attention kernel changes TP strategy

nodes.definition: Deploy a single base model server and dynamically load/unload LoRA adapters per request to serve many fine-tuned specialists without per-specialist GPU allocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vLLM LoRA serving API changes or new multi-adapter kernel released

pros.claim: Collapses N specialist GPUs to 1 base model GPU pool; linear cost saving with N specialists
pros.example: 32 domain specialists via LoRA on 4 GPUs vs 32x4=128 GPUs for separate deployments

cons.claim: LoRA adapter swap adds 5-50ms latency per cold-load; cache eviction under many adapters thrashes
cons.example: 200 adapters, LRU cache of 20: cold-start 40ms penalty on 80% requests

failure_modes: adapter weight corruption from concurrent loading
base model version drift invalidating existing adapters
LoRA rank mismatch causing silent wrong-adapter application
acceptance_tests: 100 unique adapters cycle on 1 server without OOM
adapter swap latency <20ms p95 with warm cache
output matches standalone specialist deployment within 1% on eval set
revisit_triggers: number of specialists exceeds adapter cache capacity
base model updated requiring adapter re-finetune
latency SLA tightens below adapter-swap overhead
new S-LoRA or Punica kernel available

nodes.definition: Systematically evaluate quality degradation under each quantization scheme (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) and bit-width for each specialist task to select the minimum precision that meets quality SLA.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new specialist task domain added or benchmark contamination detected

pros.claim: Systematic evaluation prevents over-quantizing specialist tasks with high precision sensitivity
pros.example: Coding specialist requires 8-bit vs summarization tolerates 4-bit

cons.claim: Evaluation cost multiplies: N specialists x M quantization configs x K benchmarks
cons.example: 10 specialists x 4 quant configs x 3 benchmarks = 120 eval runs

failure_modes: benchmark contamination inflating quantized model quality estimates
Goodhart effect: optimizing PPL but degrading task accuracy
evaluating only on easy subsets masking tail degradation
acceptance_tests: each specialist evaluated on domain-specific task benchmark
quality delta per scheme documented per specialist
selected scheme meets latency and memory targets simultaneously

nodes.definition: Implement request-driven autoscaling (replica count, batch size) and cost optimization strategies (spot instances, scale-to-zero, mixed precision) for serving specialist models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic pattern shifts or cloud GPU pricing changes materially

pros.claim: Autoscaling with scale-to-zero reduces idle GPU cost 60-90% for low-traffic specialists
pros.example: Domain expert serving 100 req/day scale-to-zero saves $1500/month vs always-on A100

cons.claim: Cold-start on scale-from-zero adds 30-120s model loading latency unacceptable for interactive use
cons.example: 7B model load from NFS: 45s cold-start on first request

failure_modes: autoscaler thrashes between 0 and 1 replica under bursty traffic
spot instance preemption during long-running request
cost model miscalculated for multi-GPU TP serving
acceptance_tests: scale-up latency <90s from zero replicas to serving
cost per 1M tokens within budget
no request dropped during scale-up event
revisit_triggers: SLA added for p99 cold-start latency

nodes.definition: Enable KV prefix caching (radix-tree or hash-based) to reuse previously computed KV states for shared prompt prefixes across requests, reducing TTFT for common system prompts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: system prompt length or diversity changes; new radix attention implementation

pros.claim: Prefix cache hit reduces TTFT from seconds to milliseconds for long shared system prompts
pros.example: 4096-token system prompt: 98% TTFT reduction on cache hit

cons.claim: Prefix cache consumes KV block pool; high diversity of prompts yields low hit rate and wasted memory
cons.example: Each user has unique prefix: 0% hit rate, 20% KV pool wasted

failure_modes: cache poisoning from prefix hash collision
stale prefix from system prompt update not invalidated
memory contention between prefix cache and decode KV blocks
acceptance_tests: cache hit rate >60% for repeated system-prompt workloads
TTFT reduction >80% on cache hit vs miss
cache invalidation correct after prefix update

nodes.definition: Deploy speculative decoding (draft model or self-speculation) to generate multiple tokens per LLM forward pass, reducing TPOT latency for high-quality specialist models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: draft model quality changes or new medusa/eagle head architecture deployed

pros.claim: Speculative decoding achieves 2-3x TPOT reduction for low-entropy specialist outputs
pros.example: Code completion with draft model achieves 2.5x speedup at 85% acceptance rate

cons.claim: Draft model must closely match target distribution; mismatch causes low acceptance rate negating speedup
cons.example: General draft model for medical specialist: 30% acceptance rate, 0.8x throughput vs baseline

failure_modes: draft model divergence on specialist domain causing throughput regression
incorrect token verification causing output drift from target model
GPU memory overhead for draft model eliminates quantization savings
acceptance_tests: acceptance rate >70% on target task distribution
TPOT latency reduction >=1.5x vs baseline
output distribution indistinguishable from target model in eval
revisit_triggers: new Medusa/EAGLE head released for base model family

nodes.definition: Select and validate hardware-specific fused dequantization+GEMM kernels (CUTLASS, ExLlamaV2, AutoGPTQ-Triton) for the target GPU to realize quantization throughput gains.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new GPU architecture (Ada/Hopper/Blackwell) or new quantization kernel release

pros.claim: Fused dequant+GEMM kernels recover 80-95% of fp16 throughput from 4-bit weights
pros.example: ExLlamaV2 Q4 kernel achieves 95% A100 fp16 MFU

cons.claim: Kernel availability varies by GPU generation; fallback to slow dequant loop eliminates quantization benefit
cons.example: A10G lacks native INT4 GEMM; AutoGPTQ falls back to fp16 dequant loop, 0.5x baseline throughput

failure_modes: kernel numerical mismatch causing silent quality degradation
CUDA version incompatibility causing kernel fallback
wrong groupsize in kernel vs quantization config
acceptance_tests: kernel throughput >=80% fp16 baseline
numerical output matches within float32 tolerance of fp16 reference
no kernel fallback warning in production logs

nodes.definition: Profile end-to-end inference latency (TTFT, TPOT, E2E) across prefill and decode phases to identify bottlenecks (memory bandwidth, compute, scheduling) and guide optimization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new serving version deployed or hardware change

pros.claim: TTFT/TPOT decomposition pinpoints whether bottleneck is prefill compute or decode memory bandwidth
pros.example: TTFT-dominated latency points to KV cache miss or long prefill; TPOT-dominated points to memory BW

cons.claim: Profiling under synthetic load may not represent real traffic mix; profiler overhead distorts measurements
cons.example: NVTX profiling adds 5-10% overhead masking true latency breakdown

failure_modes: profiling under unrepresentative batch size obscuring real bottleneck
conflating network I/O with GPU compute latency
not instrumenting scheduler wait time as separate component
acceptance_tests: TTFT and TPOT measured separately under representative load
bottleneck component identified and documented
profiling overhead <5% of measured latency

nodes.definition: Decide between local self-hosted serving (llama.cpp/vLLM on own hardware) vs hosted API (cloud inference providers) based on volume, latency, data privacy, and cost crossover.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cloud GPU spot pricing changes or privacy requirements change

pros.claim: Self-hosted breaks even vs hosted API at ~1-2M tokens/day for 7-13B models; data never leaves perimeter
pros.example: A10G spot at $0.40/hr serves 7B at 500 tok/s, breakeven vs $0.0002/tok hosted at 1.4M tok/day

cons.claim: Self-hosted requires ongoing MLOps maintenance, version management, and failure response unavoidable
cons.example: CUDA driver upgrade broke 3 models; 4h incident not reflected in $0/token cost

failure_modes: decision made on token cost alone ignoring MLOps burden
hosted API rate limits not modeled under burst traffic
privacy requirements analysis skipped for sensitive domains
acceptance_tests: TCO model includes GPU capex/opex and MLOps FTE cost
privacy requirements explicitly evaluated
breakeven token volume documented for selected model size
revisit_triggers: new provider launches competitive model API

nodes.definition: Deploy Flash Attention (Dao et al., IO-aware exact attention) to reduce attention memory complexity from O(N^2) to near-linear in sequence length, enabling long-context serving.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new Flash Attention version or GQA/MLA architecture variant deployed

pros.claim: Flash Attention 2 provides 2-4x wall-clock speedup for sequences >1k tokens vs naive attention
pros.example: FA2 on A100: 4096-token seq 3x faster, 4x less HBM traffic

cons.claim: Flash Attention requires specific GPU SM capability (SM80+); older GPUs must use fallback with memory overhead
cons.example: V100 (SM70) cannot run FA2; requires xformers or naive attention

failure_modes: attention mask incompatibility with FA2 causing incorrect causal masking
GQA/MQA head grouping bug causing wrong KV reuse
FA2 version mismatch with PyTorch version
acceptance_tests: attention output matches naive implementation within 1e-3
memory usage scales sub-quadratically beyond 4k tokens
no gradient/generation error for target sequence lengths

nodes.definition: Implement inference request routing layer that classifies incoming requests and dispatches to appropriate specialist model adapter or endpoint based on domain/task type.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new specialist domain added or routing classifier retrained

pros.claim: Correct routing to specialist vs generalist increases task accuracy 10-30% while keeping cost fixed
pros.example: Medical query routed to medical LoRA: +18% USMLE accuracy vs base model

cons.claim: Routing latency adds 5-30ms overhead per request; mis-routes reduce quality below generalist baseline
cons.example: Ambiguous query mis-routed to wrong specialist: -12% accuracy vs generalist

failure_modes: routing classifier accuracy degrades on out-of-distribution queries
routing adds unacceptable latency on critical path
no fallback when specialist unavailable causes hard error
acceptance_tests: routing accuracy >90% on held-out domain classification set
routing latency <20ms p99
graceful fallback to base model when specialist unavailable

nodes.definition: Apply INT8 weight-and-activation quantization (SmoothQuant, LLM.int8()) to achieve 2x throughput increase over fp16 with memory reduction, suitable for compute-bound scenarios.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: FP8 becomes available on target GPU replacing INT8 need

pros.claim: LLM.int8() enables 8-bit inference with near-fp16 quality via outlier decomposition
pros.example: OPT-175B in INT8 on 4 A100-80GB vs 8 needed at fp16

cons.claim: INT8 GEMM throughput advantage diminishes on memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase
cons.example: INT8 decode on A100: 1.1x vs fp16 (BW-bound), vs 1.9x on prefill (compute-bound)

failure_modes: outlier channel magnitude underestimated causing quantization error
SmoothQuant migration scale factor not fused into kernel
INT8 compute unavailable on older Turing GPUs
acceptance_tests: PPL delta <0.5 vs fp16
prefill throughput increase >=1.5x vs fp16
no overflow/NaN in INT8 GEMM

nodes.definition: Quantize KV cache tensors to FP8 or INT8 to reduce memory footprint of cached attention states, increasing effective concurrency without reducing model weight precision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vLLM adds native FP8 KV cache support or model switches to GQA

pros.claim: FP8 KV cache halves KV memory vs BF16 enabling 2x concurrent requests at long context lengths
pros.example: 4096-context FP8 KV: 2x concurrency vs BF16 on same A100

cons.claim: KV quantization error accumulates across long contexts causing generation drift
cons.example: 32k context with INT8 KV shows coherence degradation vs BF16 at turn 50+

failure_modes: KV quantization scale factor stale after dynamic range shift
generation quality degrades at long context due to accumulated quantization error
KV quant incompatible with prefix caching block sharing
acceptance_tests: generation quality delta <2% on long-context benchmarks
concurrency increase >= 1.8x at target context length
no compatibility error with prefix cache
revisit_triggers: new FP8 KV quant kernel available

nodes.definition: Establish representative load benchmarks and validate that the serving stack meets TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and availability SLAs before production promotion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving stack updated or new traffic pattern observed

pros.claim: Pre-production benchmarking catches serving regressions before they affect users
pros.example: Benchmark revealed 3x p99 latency spike from prefill/decode co-scheduling bug

cons.claim: Synthetic benchmark load may not reflect real token length distribution causing false pass
cons.example: Benchmark with fixed 512-token outputs passes; production 2048-token outputs OOM

failure_modes: benchmark input length distribution unrepresentative
SLA thresholds set without business input
availability benchmark ignores cold-start from autoscaler
acceptance_tests: p50/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT measured under realistic QPS ramp
throughput measured at target concurrency
availability SLA validated over 1-hour sustained load

nodes.definition: Convert model checkpoints between formats (safetensors, GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ) and validate compatibility with target serving framework versions to avoid silent incompatibilities.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving framework major version or new base model family released

pros.claim: Standardized safetensors format prevents weight corruption on partial write vs raw pytorch pickle
pros.example: safetensors mmap load avoids 45s torch.load pickle deserialization on every start

cons.claim: Format conversion pipelines accumulate technical debt as model families proliferate
cons.example: 5 model families x 3 formats = 15 conversion paths to maintain

failure_modes: silent weight transposition during format conversion
dtype promotion changing model behavior
tokenizer vocab mismatch between checkpoint and serving tokenizer
acceptance_tests: converted model output matches source checkpoint within 1e-4
tokenizer round-trips all special tokens correctly
model loads in target framework without error or warnings

edges.resolution_rule: evaluate both on specialist task benchmark; select higher accuracy at target bit-width; default AWQ if quality delta <1%
prefer quantization if model fits single GPU with quant; use TP only when quant insufficient for target VRAM
hosted API at low volume; self-hosted with autoscale at >1M daily tokens; document crossover explicitly

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: Maximizing batch throughput (continuous batching, large batch) conflicts with minimizing p50/p99 TTFT/TPOT for interactive use
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Set explicit TTFT and TPOT SLAs first; tune scheduler to meet latency while maximizing within those bounds

conflict_axes.name: quantization_quality_vs_compression
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive quantization (4-bit) maximizes memory savings but degrades specialist task accuracy, especially for precision-sensitive domains
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Evaluate each specialist task independently; use minimum compression that meets quality SLA per domain

conflict_axes.name: kv_memory_vs_context_length
conflict_axes.description: Long context serving requires large KV allocations competing with high-concurrency short-context serving on same GPU memory budget
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Separate serving pools for long-context and short-context workloads; use KV quantization for long-context pool

conflict_axes.name: lora_adapter_count_vs_cache_efficiency
conflict_axes.description: More specialist LoRA adapters increases routing flexibility but exceeds adapter cache capacity, increasing cold-load latency
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Limit hot adapters to cache size; consolidate low-traffic specialists; measure hit rate to justify cache expansion

conflict_axes.name: tensor_parallelism_vs_quantization
conflict_axes.description: Tensor parallelism enables fp16 quality across GPUs but costs proportionally more than quantization to single GPU
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Default to 4-bit quantization; only use TP when quantization quality is unacceptable for the specialist task

conflict_axes.name: local_serving_cost_vs_hosted_api
conflict_axes.description: Self-hosted GPU serving breaks even at high volume but requires MLOps investment; hosted API is efficient at low volume but expensive at scale
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Compute TCO including MLOps FTE; set volume crossover point; re-evaluate quarterly

conflict_axes.name: speculative_decoding_draft_quality_vs_overhead
conflict_axes.description: Draft model must closely match target distribution or low acceptance rate negates speedup; domain specialist targets often diverge from general draft models
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Measure acceptance rate on domain traffic before committing; use Medusa heads on same model family to avoid distribution mismatch

conflict_axes.name: prefix_cache_memory_vs_prompt_diversity
conflict_axes.description: Prefix caching provides TTFT gains only when prompts are repetitive; diverse user prompts yield near-zero hit rate while consuming KV memory
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Measure prefix hit rate on target traffic; disable prefix cache if hit rate <30%; use separate pool for shared system prompts

conflict_axes.name: autoscale_cost_vs_cold_start_latency
conflict_axes.description: Scale-to-zero minimizes idle GPU cost but creates model loading cold-start latency incompatible with interactive SLAs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Maintain minimum 1 warm replica for interactive traffic; scale-to-zero only for batch/async endpoints

edge_cases.description: Quantized 4-bit specialist model shows near-fp16 PPL but catastrophic degradation on rare domain vocabulary not well represented in calibration set
edge_cases.mitigation: Include domain-specific calibration data; run full task-accuracy evaluation not just PPL

edge_cases.description: LoRA adapter rank too low for complex specialist task; base model dominates and adapter has minimal effect—misdiagnosed as routing failure
edge_cases.mitigation: Verify adapter weight magnitude and task delta before routing evaluation; use rank >=64 for complex tasks

edge_cases.description: Flash Attention with GQA model and PagedAttention simultaneously requires correct KV head grouping in block table; mismatch causes silent wrong-token attention
edge_cases.mitigation: Validate GQA head grouping in paged block table with deterministic attention test suite

edge_cases.description: Tensor parallel degree not divisible into model head count causes unequal shards; padding or weight replication required causing silent memory overuse
edge_cases.mitigation: Verify TP degree divides number of attention heads and MLP hidden dim; document per-architecture TP constraints

edge_cases.description: Speculative decoding with continuous batching causes variable-length batch verification; incorrect prefix sharing between different requests corrupts generation
edge_cases.mitigation: Disable speculative decoding if acceptance rate <60% or under heavy concurrent load; validate per-request isolation

edge_cases.description: KV cache quantization accumulates error over long dialogue turns; quality acceptable at turn 5 but incoherent at turn 50 in multi-turn specialist deployment
edge_cases.mitigation: Evaluate KV quantization quality on long multi-turn dialogues specifically; set turn-count quality checkpoints

edge_cases.description: Autoscaler spins up new replica but cold model load takes 90s; load balancer routes requests to not-ready replica causing 90s timeout cascade
edge_cases.mitigation: Implement readiness probe gated on first successful inference; configure LB health check before routing to new replica

edge_cases.description: GPTQ calibration on generic data for model serving medical specialist causes vocabulary outlier channels to be unprotected; INT4 inference corrupts medical terminology tokens
edge_cases.mitigation: Always use domain-matched calibration data for specialist models; verify accuracy on held-out domain benchmark post-quantization

edge_cases.description: Prefix cache invalidation not triggered after system prompt update; stale KV blocks serve outdated prompt causing behavioral regression undetected until user reports
edge_cases.mitigation: Tie prefix cache invalidation to prompt version hash; test cache invalidation in deployment pipeline

edge_cases.description: Model format conversion transposes weight matrix silently producing non-NaN valid but wrong outputs; catches only on task-accuracy test not PPL
edge_cases.mitigation: Validate converted model output against source model on fixed prompt set; compare token logits not just PPL

edge_cases.description: vLLM LoRA serving silently applies wrong adapter when adapter name hash collides; extremely rare but causes user data cross-contamination in multi-tenant deployment
edge_cases.mitigation: Use full UUID not truncated hash for adapter identity; verify adapter name space collisions at registration time

edge_cases.description: GGUF quantization on ARM CPU uses NEON backend that lacks Q4_K_M support; falls back to slow Q8_0 without warning; throughput 2x lower than expected
edge_cases.mitigation: Verify SIMD backend capability at startup; document per-architecture quantization tier support matrix

workflow.action: Define serving SLA (TTFT, TPOT, throughput, availability) and hardware budget
Assess model size vs GPU VRAM and decide quantization or tensor-parallelism strategy
Convert model checkpoint to target format (safetensors/GGUF/GPTQ/AWQ)
Evaluate quantization quality delta per specialist on task benchmarks
workflow.gate: all specialist quality deltas within SLA

workflow.action: Configure serving framework (vLLM/TGI/llama.cpp): batching, KV cache, Flash Attention, TP degree
workflow.gate: serving starts without error; first inference correct

workflow.action: Validate quantization kernel throughput on target GPU; confirm no fallback to slow dequant path
Enable prefix caching and LoRA hot-swap; configure adapter registry and routing classifier
workflow.gate: routing accuracy >90% on held-out set; adapter swap <20ms p95

workflow.action: Profile TTFT/TPOT under representative load; identify prefill vs decode bottleneck
workflow.gate: p99 TTFT and TPOT within SLA

workflow.action: Optionally enable KV cache quantization and/or speculative decoding; re-benchmark
Configure autoscaling policy and cost model; set scale-to-zero for batch endpoints only
Run full SLA validation benchmark and sign off for production promotion
workflow.gate: all SLA checks pass; human reviewer signs off

dominance_rules.condition: model fits on single GPU at 4-bit GPTQ/AWQ AND quality delta <3% on specialist task
dominance_rules.rationale: quantization is lower cost and simpler than TP; use TP only when quality unacceptable

dominance_rules.condition: traffic volume <1M tokens/day for specialist endpoint
dominance_rules.rationale: MLOps burden exceeds cost saving below breakeven volume

dominance_rules.condition: N specialists > 10 AND specialists share same base model family
dominance_rules.rationale: LoRA hot-swap saves N-1 GPU servers; cost linear in N

dominance_rules.condition: system prompt length > 1024 tokens AND prompt reuse rate > 50%
dominance_rules.rationale: TTFT reduction >80% on cache hit; cost is KV memory only

dominance_rules.condition: serving GPU is H100/A100 AND Flash Attention 2 compatible model
dominance_rules.rationale: FA2 always faster and lower memory; no quality tradeoff

dominance_rules.condition: specialist task acceptance rate on draft model >70%
dominance_rules.rationale: Speculative decoding dominates standard decode in TPOT when acceptance rate >70%

dominance_rules.condition: deployment target is CPU or hybrid CPU+GPU with <16GB GPU VRAM
dominance_rules.rationale: GGUF llama.cpp is the only viable serving option for CPU/hybrid targets

dominance_rules.condition: context length >16k AND GPU is memory-bandwidth bound during decode
dominance_rules.rationale: FP8 KV cache halves KV BW pressure; quality loss acceptable beyond 16k context

dominance_rules.condition: calibration data does not cover specialist domain vocabulary
dominance_rules.rationale: Specialist domain vocabulary mis-quantization cannot be detected by PPL alone
Scale-to-zero cold-start 30-120s violates interactive TTFT SLA

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize quantization scheme before task-accuracy evaluation on all specialist domains
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering quality regression after deployment causing re-quantization

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not configure LoRA serving before validating adapter hot-swap latency on production hardware
anti_rework_rules.prevents: SLA violation from cold-load latency discovered in production

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not promote to production without running benchmark under realistic sequence length distribution
anti_rework_rules.prevents: benchmark passing on synthetic short requests while real workload OOMs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply tensor parallelism before verifying head count divisibility by TP degree for target model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silent silent padding or weight replication causing memory overuse or wrong output

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not enable speculative decoding without measuring acceptance rate on target domain traffic first
anti_rework_rules.prevents: throughput regression from low-acceptance draft model on specialist distribution

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not merge base model update without re-validating all LoRA adapters against new base version
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silent quality degradation from adapter/base version mismatch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip domain-matched calibration data when quantizing specialist models
anti_rework_rules.prevents: outlier-channel miscalibration causing domain-vocabulary corruption at 4-bit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change prefix caching configuration without testing invalidation behavior after prompt update
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stale KV blocks serving outdated system prompt undetected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not make local-vs-hosted decision based on token cost alone; include MLOps FTE in TCO
anti_rework_rules.prevents: underestimating self-hosted total cost leading to budget overrun

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy quantized model without validating quantization kernel availability and throughput on target GPU
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kernel fallback to slow dequantization path negating quantization benefit

iteration_protocol.trigger: TTFT exceeds SLA after initial deployment
TPOT exceeds SLA under target concurrency
Specialist quality regression detected after quantization
actions: re-run task accuracy eval per specialist

iteration_protocol.trigger: LoRA adapter cache hit rate falls below 30%
actions: increase cache size if GPU memory allows
retrain routing classifier on updated request distribution
add fallback to base model for low-confidence routes
move low-traffic specialists to hosted API
increase quantization to reduce GPU count

priority_rationale: SERVE_ARCH first as all else depends on framework choice. KV_CACHE and CONT_BATCH next as they determine throughput ceiling. BENCH_SERVE early to establish SLA gates. QUANT_QUALITY before specific quant methods to set evaluation criteria. LORA_HOTSWAP and ROUTER_DISPATCH critical for multi-specialist orchestration. Quantization methods (GPTQ/AWQ) follow. FLASH_ATTN and QUANT_KERNEL as enabling optimizations. TENSOR_PARA high complexity, needed only when quantization insufficient. Profiling, hosting decisions, advanced optimizations (PREFIX_CACHE, SPECULATIVE, KV_QUANT) follow. GGUF and MODEL_FORMAT last as narrower scope.
